1.n: demonstrative ὥς = οὕτως; the digitized text prints ὧς with a circumflex, its only one in the Odyssey, where the formula has ὣς (4.511, 6.1, 344); the Iliad's text prints ὧς in καὶ ὧς, οὐδʼ ὧς (Iliad 1.116, 12.432); the verse follows 6.1 (= 344), with ἠρᾶτο for καθεῦδε
Odysseus, named at the end of the line
= ἔνθα; in the grove of Athena outside the city (6.321–322)
contracted impf. (= ἠράετο); his prayer to Athena, 6.323–327

2.n: Ionic κούρη = κόρη: Nausicaa, driving home from the river (6.316–320)
μένος with a genitive, 'the might of', a periphrasis for the mules themselves, as μένος Ἀλκινόοιο (167, 178) for the king
epic gen./dat. dual -οιιν: the pair of mules, as 6.82

3.n: possessive ὅς (= ἑοῦ), not the relative: 'her own'
intensive ἀγα- + κλυτός 'famous'; ἀγακλυτὰ δώματα again 46, as 3.388
= δώματα, aspirated before ἱ-; plural of one house; accusative of the goal
epic ἱκάνω = ἱκνέομαι 'come to, reach', + acc.

4.n: unaugmented transitive 1st aorist (= ἔστησε): the mules understood, as ἵππους στήσασα Iliad 5.755 (Merry on 7.4)
epic dat. pl. -οισι; plural of one entrance, as 4.20
epic μιν = αὐτήν; with ἀμφίς: 'around her'

5.n: used as a noun; dative with ἐναλίγκιοι
relative, accented before enclitic ῥʼ: 'and they'
= ὑπό; + gen. 'from under': loosed from the wagon's yoke

6.n: feminine, as αἱ (6.83) and τάς (6.89) of these mules
collective: 'clothing', the washing of Book 6; accent from enclitic τε

7.n: unaugmented (= ἔδαιε); transitive 'make blaze'; the subject is γρῆυς (8); at evening the fire gave light, warmth or both (Merry on 7.7)

8.n: Ionic γρηῦς (Attic γραῦς), printed with the accent γρῆυς; subject of δαῖε (7)

'of Apeire' (Ἀπείρηθεν 9), a land known only from this passage; the scholia explain it as 'from far away' or 'from Epirus', but it is as mythical as Hypereia (6.4), a land 'of which the limits are unknown' (Merry on 7.8); only here in Homer
'chamber-servant' (θάλαμος + -πολος, as ἀμφίπολος); for the form in -η- Merry on 7.8 cites Monro's Homeric Grammar §124a; again 23.293, of Eurynome
Nausicaa's old nurse (12), known only from this passage

9.n: article used as relative (= ἥν); accent from enclitic ποτʼ
Ἀπείρη with the suffix -θεν 'from', printed as one word, as Ἴδηθεν 'from Ida' in the Iliad; only here in Homer
reduplicated aorist; she was a captive, taken in a raid
epithet of ships: 'curved at both ends' (or 'rowed on both sides')

10.n: emphatic: her, out of all the captives (Merry on 7.10)
predicate: 'as a prize of honor', as Hecamede was chosen out for Nestor (Iliad 11.627)
unaugmented (= ἐξεῖλον): 'chose out' as a prize of honor; the subject, the Phaeacians, is understood

11.n: genitive with ἄκουεν: 'the people hearkened to him as to a god' (Merry on 7.11)
postpositive ὡς 'like', accented after its noun

12.n: ὅς used as demonstrative, as ἥ (13): 'she', Eurymedusa (Merry on 7.12–13)
unaugmented (= ἔτρεφε): she was Nausicaa's nurse, who kept a place of intimacy and trust in a Greek household (Merry on 7.12)

13.n: demonstrative, as ἣ (12); Zenodotus rejected the line as repeating δαῖε δέ οἱ πῦρ (7) (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 7.13)
contracted (= ἐκόσμεε): 'set in order', i.e. laid out; contrast ἀπεκόσμεον ἔντεα δαιτός (232) (Merry on 7.13)

14.n: = πόλινδε, elided: πόλις with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word; πόλινδʼ ἴμεν as 6.255

in tmesis with χεῦε (15) (ἀμφιχέω 'pour around'); Merry prints αὐτὰρ Ἀθήνη: ἀμφὶ δʼ Ἀθήνη is the reading of two manuscripts and of Macrobius' quotation, adopted by Ameis (Merry's critical note on 7.14)

15.n: with ἠέρα: 'a thick mist', as Iliad 17.269–270; again 140

epic ἠήρ, feminine in Homer: 'mist, haze', not 'air'; a mist that hides him from sight; in the Iliad, Nitzsch held, the gods use it only to hide themselves, in the Odyssey for their favorites too, but compare Iliad 5.345 (Merry on 7.15)
in tmesis: ἀμφὶ … χεῦε (14) = ἀμφέχευε; unaugmented epic aorist
φίλα φρονεῖν 'think in friendship', 'be friendly', + dat., as 75 (= 6.313) and Iliad 4.219

15.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

15.n: single σ; epic dat. -ῆϊ; dative with φίλα φρονέουσα

16.n: 'lest', with the optatives κερτομέοι and ἐξερέοιτο (17) after the past χεῦε

16.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

17.n: uncontracted optative: 'taunt, mock'; optative of purpose after μή (16) in past time
= ἐξερέοιτο, aspirated before ὅ-; from epic ἐξερέομαι 'inquire', uncontracted, as 4.119

17.p: indef. rel. pron. · nom. sg. masc.
17.n: epic ὅτις = ὅστις, in an indirect question
optative of the indirect question in past time

18.n: 'lovely', from ἐράω 'love', for ἐρασ-νός, the σ assimilated (Merry on 7.18); elsewhere only of Calydon, Iliad 9.531, 9.577

19.n: 'then, there', opening the main clause after ὅτε (18)

20.n: = παρθένος 'maiden', formed from it as ὀρφανικός from ὀρφανός; taken either as a noun in apposition to νεήνιδι or as an adjective agreeing with it (Merry on 7.20); again 11.39 and Iliad 18.567

20.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

20.n: Ionic νεῆνις = νεᾶνις 'girl'; elsewhere in Homer only Iliad 18.418 (νεήνισιν)
'water jar' (kept apart from πρόχοος 'pitcher', 7.172); only here in Homer

20.p: verb · pres. part. act. dat. sg. fem.

22.n: 'child', a kindly address to a girl
οὐκ ἄν + optative: a polite request, 'will you not …?'
with the potential optative ἡγήσαιο; Aristophanes read ἦ ῥά μοι, more likely ἦ ῥά νύ μοι, Merry suggests (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 7.22)
dative with ἡγήσαιο: 'lead the way for me'
epic ἀνέρος = ἀνδρός; Ἀλκινόου (23) explains it, as ἐξ ἀπίης γαίης explains τηλόθεν (25) (Merry on 7.25)
potential optative with ἄν; + dat. of the person led

24.n: 'much-suffering', as 6.193: Aristarchus took it as = ταλαίπωρος, others as 'come from afar' (scholia on this line, in Merry on 6.193)
present with perfect sense: 'I am come'

25.n: τῆλε 'far' with the suffix -θεν 'from'; ἐξ ἀπίης γαίης explains it: 'from afar, from a distant land' (Merry on 7.25); τηλόθεν ἐξ ἀπίης γαίης as Iliad 1.270, ἐξ ἀπίης γαίης also 3.49
Ionic fem. -ης; 'far-off' (ἀπό); the accent made Merry doubt that derivation and suggest 'a land over the water'; Ἀπία, a name of the Peloponnese, is a different word (Buttmann, in Merry on 7.25)

26.n: for γαῖαν ἔχουσιν a scholium and Eustathius record ἔργα νέμονται (Merry's critical note on 7.26)

28.n: epic τοι = σοι; dative with δείξω (29)
ξεῖνε πάτερ, the respectful address of the young to an older man; again 48, 8.145, 17.553
object of an understood δεῖξαι: 'which you bid me (show)'; κελεύεις … πεφραδέμεν in full at 48–49

29.n: genitive with ἐγγύθι: Athena speaks as a Phaeacian girl whose father lives by the palace

30.n: dative of manner; σιγῇ τοῖον as 4.776
adverbial with σιγῇ: 'just so, quite silently'
'lead, guide', + acc. of the way; ἐγὼ δʼ ὁδὸν ἡγεμονεύσω as 6.261 (Nausicaa)

31.n: accent from enclitic τινʼ; with the imperatives
uncontracted imperative -εο (= -ου); epic προτί (= πρός) + ὄσσομαι 'look': 'look at', as Iliad 22.356
imperative of epic ἐρεείνω 'ask, question' (not the unaugmented imperfect, as 5.85)

32.n: with μάλα: 'not much', i.e. not at all (Merry on 7.32)

'the people here': the common Phaeacians a stranger meets in the street, of whom Nausicaa too had warned (6.273–275), not Alcinous and his chiefs, who welcome him (159–166, 186 ff.); Nitzsch's view, that Athena voices Odysseus' own wary thoughts, Merry finds too subtle (Merry on 7.32)
= μάλα; οὐ … μάλα 'not over and above fond of', meaning 'not at all fond of' (Merry on 7.32)
middle 'bear, endure', + acc.: stronger than 'are not hospitable to' (Merry on 7.32)

33.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
33.n: middle, as 17.35, 21.224; 'welcome warmly', as the active ἀγαπαζέμεν Iliad 24.464
= φιλέουσι, uncontracted (Attic φιλοῦσι); of a guest 'entertain, make welcome', as 4.29
ὅς κε + subjunctive: 'whoever', a general relative clause
the reading of Bekker and La Roche, where most manuscripts have ἔλθοι; a scholium quoting the line on 13.119 gives ὅτε κέν τις ἵκηται (Merry's critical note on 7.33)

34.n: epic νηυσί = ναυσί; dative with πεποιθότες
epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν); the fixed epithet, where ὠκείῃσι is the special one (Merry on 7.34)

34.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

34.n: epic dat. pl. -ῃσι; Ionic fem. ὠκεῖα; the two epithets are tautological only in words: 'trusting in the speed of their swift ships' (Merry on 7.34)

35.n: 'the depth, gulf' of the sea; μέγα λαῖτμα as 4.504, Iliad 19.267
= δῶκε, unaugmented (= ἔδωκε); the gift, their seamanship, is understood
'shaker of the earth' (ἔνοσις 'shaking' + χθών 'earth'): Poseidon, the father of their first king (56–62)

36.n: ὡς εἰ 'as if', with no verb, as 19.39 (Merry on 7.36)
the simile at full length in Iliad 15.80–83, Hera flying as swift as the thought of a man who has traveled far (Merry on 7.36)

37.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

38.n: epic gen. -οιο; θεός of a goddess

39.n: 'famed for ships' (ναῦς + κλυτός), as ναυσικλειτός (6.22); the text accents ναυσικλυτοί here, ναυσίκλυτοι elsewhere (8.191, 8.369, 13.166, 16.227), of the Phaeacians, and of the Phoenicians (15.415)

40.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. sg. masc.

40.n: + acc. 'through the midst of' them, of his way through the crowd; with the genitive (διʼ αὐτῶν 10.391) the picture differs slightly (Merry on 7.40)

41.n: contracted (= εἴαε); with οὐ (40): 'would not allow'
printed here without the diaeresis; of Athena only here, who in the Iliad is ἠΰκομος (6.92, 6.273, 6.303) (Merry on 7.41); ἐυπλόκαμος, δεινὴ θεός again of Calypso (246, 255) and Circe (10.136)
'dread, to be feared'; δεινὴ θεός of Athena also Iliad 6.380, 6.385
enclitic form of ἄρα; accent from enclitic οἱ
Odysseus; dative with κατέχευε (42); Zenodotus read ἥ σφισιν 'over them', wrongly, since 143 shows the mist around Odysseus alone (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 7.41)

42.n: Ionic -ην; 'divine, wondrous', with ἀχλύν (41), as Iliad 20.342
epic aorist ἔχευα: 'poured down, shed', + dat. (οἱ 41)

42.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

43.n: unaugmented (= ἐθαύμαζεν); the imperfect of a wonder renewed at each new sight (Merry on 7.43)
the harbors on either side of the city (6.263)

44.n: 'of the heroes themselves', turning from the city to its people (Merry on 7.44)
the word means both the speaking and the place of assembly (Merry on 7.44); the Phaeacians' ἀγορή lies by the temple of Poseidon (6.266)
uncontracted (Attic τείχη); the wall Nausithous drew round the city (6.9)

45.n: epic dat. pl. -εσσι(ν); a palisade along the top of the walls, as on the Achaean wall (Iliad 12.55–56); in the Odyssey only here (Merry on 7.45)

45.p: verb · pf. part. act. acc. pl. neut.
45.n: intransitive perfect ἄρηρα 'be fitted', + dat.; σκολόπεσσιν … ἠρήρει of the Achaean wall, Iliad 12.55–56
in apposition: 'a wonder to see', as 6.306 and Iliad 5.725

46.n: = δώματα, aspirated before ἱ-; plural of one house; accusative of the goal

47.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι; plural though she speaks to one man, as 5.202 (Merry on 7.47); the line = Iliad 5.420
δέ of the apodosis, after ὅτε (46): 'then'

48.n: epic τοι = σοι, ethic dative: 'here, you see, is …'
object of πεφραδέμεν (49); the line begins as 28

49.n: reduplicated aorist (πέφραδον) of φράζω, epic infinitive -έμεν (= πεφραδεῖν): 'point out, show'
uncontracted acc. pl. -έας; 'nurtured by Zeus', of kings, as Iliad 2.445

epic acc. pl. -ῆας; the Phaeacian lords, twelve beside Alcinous (8.390–391); with δαινυμένους (50) as the Cadmeans Tydeus found feasting (Iliad 4.385–386), and like Tydeus he is not to be afraid (Merry on 7.49)

50.n: acc. of the by-form δαίτη (as δαίτης 3.44); cognate accusative with δαινυμένους, as βουλὰς βουλεύειν 6.61 (Merry on 7.50)

50.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. pl. masc.

50.n: accent from enclitic τι; with τάρβει (51)

51.n: comparative of ἀγαθός; predicate with τελέθει (52)

52.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); Bekker and others reject the line, which spoils the maxim's general force: it is more pointed ending at ἀμείνων (51) (Merry's critical note on 7.52)
poetic 'come to be, be': a general truth
εἰ καί 'even if'; accent from enclitic ποθεν
enclitic: 'from somewhere'; ποθεν ἄλλοθεν 'from some other place'; a scholium records the reading εἰ καὶ μάλα τηλόθεν (Merry's critical note on 7.52)

53.n: 'mistress' of the house: Arete; not found in the Iliad, since the relation is a domestic one (Merry on 7.53); ἄλοχος δέσποινα 3.403
neuter plural as adverb; with δέσποιναν: she will be the first his eye rests on in the hall, the person whose suppliant he will be (Merry on 7.53)
uncontracted 2 sg. -εαι (= κιχήσῃ); a plain future, 'find', not 'approach' or 'make suit to' (Merry on 7.53)

54.n: wife and niece of Alcinous (63–66), first named here; the scholia take the name as 'prayed for' (ἀρητός), born in answer to prayer (Merry on 7.54)
= ὄνομα; nominative, not an accusative of respect: 'Arete is her name', as 9.366, 19.409, 24.306 (Merry on 7.54)
'given with a meaning', properly of a name added for a reason, as Alcyone, Iliad 9.562 (Merry on 7.54); two-termination adjective
ἐκ … τοκήων τῶν αὐτῶν 'of the same parents'
epic gen. pl. -ήων (Attic τοκέων); here ancestors, not parents: she is Alcinous' niece as well as his wife (Merry on 7.54)

56.n: object of γείνατο (57); son of Poseidon and Periboea, who led the Phaeacians to Scheria (6.7–10)

57.n: unaugmented (= ἐγείνατο): 'begot, bore', with the father and the mother as subjects
mother of Nausithous by Poseidon, youngest daughter of Eurymedon (58), known only from this passage; another Periboea is the mother of Pelegon (Iliad 21.142)
accusative of respect; εἶδος ἀρίστη as Iliad 2.715
superlative of ἀγαθός: 'best', with εἶδος 'most beautiful'

58.n: king of the Giants (59), known only from this passage; not Agamemnon's charioteer (Iliad 4.228) or Nestor's attendant (Iliad 8.114, 11.620)

59.n: elided ποτε; τ → θ before the rough breathing of ὑπερ-
epic dat. pl. -οισι; 'high-spirited'; with ἀτάσθαλον (60) the epithet suggests to Merry that the Giants perished in some foolhardy war (Merry on 7.59)

epic dat. pl. -εσσι(ν); dative with βασίλευεν; in Homer a mortal people, as Pausanias observes (8.29.2), not the earth-born monsters of the later war against the gods (Merry on 7.59); again 206 (with the Cyclopes), 10.120

60.n: transitive aorist 'destroyed, brought to ruin'; how is not told: in a foolhardy war, by a rising of his people, or through his own guilt (Merry on 7.59)

61.n: 2nd aorist passive of μίσγω 'mingle': 'lay with', + dat.

62.n: unaugmented (= ἤνασσε); with ἐν + dat., 'ruled among'

63.n: Arete's father (64–66, 146), killed by Apollo; the name is the Iliad's epithet ῥηξήνωρ 'breaker of men' (of Achilles, Iliad 7.228); second accent from enclitic τʼ

64.n: 'without male issue' (ἀ- + κοῦρος), only here in Homer; with νυμφίον (65), 'before his bridal days were over', explained by μίαν οἴην παῖδα λιπόντα (65); Nauck's ἄωρον, 'cut off untimely', is needless (Merry on 7.64)

64.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

64.n: = βάλε, unaugmented (= ἔβαλε): a sudden death by Apollo's arrows, as 3.279–280

65.n: 'newly married', as Iliad 23.223: he had been married long enough for a daughter to be born, unless Arete was born after his death (Merry on 7.64)

65.p: verb · aor. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

66.n: = ποιήσατο, unaugmented (= ἐποιήσατο); middle 'made (her) his own'
predicate accusative: he married his brother's daughter

68.n: epic -σσ-: 'as many as', i.e. of all the women who

69.n: adverbial 'exceedingly', with κῆρι a locative dative: 'with all their hearts', as 5.36 (Merry on 7.69)
perfect passive: 'has been honored'; second accent from enclitic τε

'and is (so)': Nauck calls the words corrupt, though the manuscripts have no variant (Merry's critical note on 7.69); Nitzsch supplies τιμήεσσα 'honored', Merry would rather repeat περί, 'and is above all' in worth, as 1.66; the construction of τετίμηται resumes in ἐκ … (70) (Merry on 7.69)

70.n: of the agent with the passive τετίμηται (69), as ἐφίληθεν ἐκ Διός Iliad 2.668–669 (Merry on 7.69); accent from enclitic τε

71.n: epic μιν = αὐτήν; accent from enclitic ῥα; object of εἰσορόωντες and of δειδέχαται (72)
θεός of a goddess; θεὸν ὣς εἰσορόωσιν of a fine speaker, 8.173
postpositive ὡς 'like', accented after its noun

71.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

72.n: perfect from the root of δείκνυμι, with the pluperfects δείδεκτο Iliad 9.224, δειδέχατο Iliad 4.4 (Merry on 7.72): 'greet'; Ionic 3 pl. -αται; present in sense
epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν): 'welcome with loyal speeches' (Merry on 7.72)
= στείχῃσι, epic subjunctive -ῃσι; without κε in a general temporal clause

73.n: καὶ αὐτή 'she herself too', in her own right, not only by light reflected from the king (Merry on 7.73)

74.n: relative, epic dat. pl. -ῃσι: 'for the women to whom she is well disposed'; the more graceful reading, Eustathius says, who also records ᾗσιν ἐυφροσύνῃσι, 'by her own good sense'; Merry prints οἷσιν, 'for those she favors, be they even men', as some scholia take it (Merry on 7.74 and critical note)
= τε; explanatory rather than copulative: the proof of her good sense (73) (Merry on 7.74)
epic ἐΰ = εὖ; ἐὺ φρονεῖν + dat. 'be well disposed to', not 'give wise counsel' (Merry on 7.74)
epic subjunctive -ῃσι; without κε in a general relative clause

75.n: accent from enclitic κεν; 75–76 = 6.313–314 (Nausicaa's advice), 77 after 6.315
accent from enclitic τοι; εἰ κε + subjunctive
epic τοι = σοι; dative with φίλα φρονέῃσι
φίλα φρονεῖν 'think in friendship', 'be friendly', + dat., as 15 and Iliad 4.219

76.n: 'hope' (cf. ἐλπίς); ἐστί understood; always ἐλπωρή τοι ἔπειτα (2.280, 6.314, 23.287)
+ acc. of the place reached, with ἐς (77)

77.n: the line as 5.42 (Zeus of Odysseus), with σήν for ἑήν; 6.315 has οἶκον ἐυκτίμενον

78.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

79.n: the passage (79–80) was suspected, as Chaeris says in his Corrections (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 7.79–80): perhaps, Merry thinks, as added by a later rhapsode to please Athenian feeling
= ἐπί; + acc. of the space crossed: 'over the sea'

80.n: in Attica, northeast of Athens; named only here in Homer
the city, not the goddess: in Homer only here in the singular, elsewhere the plural Ἀθῆναι (Iliad 2.546; 3.278, 3.307)

81.n: unaugmented imperfect of the by-form δύνω; + acc. 'went into'
epic gen. -ῆος; his house is the temple on the Acropolis that he shares with Athena, as Iliad 2.547–549, and Herodotus 8.55 (Merry on 7.81)

82.n: dative of possession with κῆρ; ἱσταμένῳ (83) agrees with it

83.p: verb · pres. part. mid. dat. sg. masc.
83.n: intransitive middle, agreeing with οἱ (82): catching glimpses of the palace, he stopped again and again in wonder (Merry on 7.83)

84.n: ὥς τε 'just as'; accent from enclitic τε; short for αἴγλη πέλεν ὥς τε ἠελίου αἴγλη; the line = 4.45, of Menelaus' palace, which Nitzsch thinks the more splendid (Merry on 7.84)

85.n: the line as 4.46, with μεγαλήτορος Ἀλκινόοιο for Μενελάου κυδαλίμοιο
= κατά; τ → θ before rough breathing
epic gen. -οιο; μεγαλήτορος Ἀλκινόοιο again 93, as 6.17

86.n: the walls of the court (αὐλή), not of the house, which is described from 95; θριγκός (87) belongs to open-air walls, as 17.266–267 (Merry on 7.86)

= ἐληλέδατο, pluperfect passive with Ionic 3 pl. -ατο and an inserted δ: 'had been driven', i.e. carried along in a line, as ἐλαύνειν ὄγμον Iliad 11.68; the best-attested reading, against ἐληλάδατο, ἐληλέατο and ἐρηρέδατο (as 95) (Merry on 7.86 and critical note)
ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα 'this way and that', lengthwise and across (Merry on 7.96)

87.n: 'the inmost part', here the inner end of the court (Merry on 7.86)
adverbial 'round about', along the top of the walls
'coping, cornice' along the top of a wall; again 17.267 (θριγκοῖσι), and the verb ἐθρίγκωσεν 14.10
epic gen. -οιο; genitive of material: κύανος, not here lapis lazuli or steel but most likely a glass paste or enamel colored blue, laid as a frieze, like the plates found at Mycenae (Merry on 7.87)

88.n: plural of the two leaves of the door
epic ἐέργω = εἴργω; with ἐντός 'shut in, enclosed'

90.n: = ἐπί, aspirated before ὑ-; adverbial: 'on (them)', above the doorposts
Ionic fem. -έη (Attic χρυσῆ); predicate, ἦν understood
the curved handle on the outside of the door, by which it was pulled to, as 1.441

91.n: epic χρύσειος = χρύσεος; images of dogs, spoken of as living things, as Homer speaks of works of art in terms of what they copy (Merry on 7.91)

92.p: verb · pf. part. act. dat. pl. fem.
92.n: epic fem. participle ἰδυῖα (= εἰδυῖα): 'knowing, skilled'; ἰδυίῃσι πραπίδεσσι of Hephaestus' work, as Iliad 1.608, 18.380

94.n: with οὕς (92), the dogs; ἀθάνατος καὶ ἀγήρως ἤματα πάντα as Iliad 8.539

94.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. pl. masc.
94.n: the short (Attic) form, in this text again only 19.489 (οὔσης); Merry counts ὄντες at 19.230 too, where this text reads ἐόντες; Nitzsch doubts that ἐόντας could stand here as two syllables (Merry on 7.94)
contracted from ἀγήραος; ἀθάνατος καὶ ἀγήρως as 5.218
accusative of duration: ἤματα πάντα 'all their days'

95.n: adverbial: 'within', in the men's hall (Merry on 7.95)
= ἐρηρέδατο, pluperfect of ἐρείδω 'prop, fix', with Ionic 3 pl. -ατο and an inserted δ: 'were set firmly'; a scholium reads ἐληλέδατʼ here too, as at 86 (Merry's critical note on 7.95)

96.n: 'right through, the whole way round' (Merry on 7.96)
'cloths, coverings', as those spread over the chariots, Iliad 5.194

97.n: Ionic 3 pl. -ατο (= ἐβέβληντο), unaugmented: 'had been thrown, lay spread'
in apposition to πέπλοι: women's weaving

98.n: epic diectasis (= ἑδριῶντο), unaugmented: 'sat', of their habit

99.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
99.n: πίνοντες καὶ ἔδοντες, as πίνοντας καὶ ἔδοντας· ἐπηετανὸν γὰρ ἔχουσιν 10.427

99.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

99.n: neuter as a noun, 'unfailing store', or adverbially, 'in unfailing plenty', as 128 (Merry on 7.99, referring to 4.89); Hesychius glosses it 'continuous, unceasing, plentiful'

100.n: epic χρύσειος = χρύσεος; statues of boys, like the dogs (91) (Merry on 7.91)
here 'pedestals', properly anything one mounts (βαίνω), as the stand for chariots, Iliad 8.441 (Merry on 7.100); a scholium condemns the reading βουνῶν (Merry's critical note on 7.100)

101.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. pl. fem.

101.n: 'among, between': the torch grasped in both hands (Merry on 7.100)

101.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

102.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

102.n: accusative of duration: 'through the nights' (Merry on 7.102)
epic dat. pl. -εσσι; dative of interest

103.n: the same number of women serve in Odysseus' house (22.421) (Merry on 7.103)

104.n: 'grind' (ἀλέω), only here in Homer; ἀλετρίς 'grinding woman' 20.105
epic dat. pl. -ῃς (= μύλαις): 'at the mills', the hand mills of 20.105–111; Merry prints μύλης, 'at the mill', and records μύλῃς and μύλοις (Merry's critical note on 7.104)
accent thrown back (anastrophe): placed after its noun
'apple-hued', i.e. yellow, of ripe grain; others connect it with a word for 'white, glistening' (Merry on 7.104); only here in Homer

105.n: ἱστός 'loom' (also 'mast'); object of ὑφόωσι: 'weave at the looms'
epic diectasis of a by-form ὑφάω (= ὑφῶσι), only here in Homer
'the wool on the distaff, yarn'; ἠλάκατα στρωφῶσα 6.53, 6.306

106.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. fem.

106.n: adverbial 'like'; second accent from enclitic τε; the point is the restless movement of their hands, like the quivering leaves of the aspen, not their number or closeness, as Nitzsch held; the scholia give both views (Merry on 7.106)
epic gen. -οιο; the black poplar or aspen

107.n: contracted from καιροεσσέων (καιρόεις, from καῖρος, the loop holding each warp thread on the loom): 'close-woven' (Merry on 7.107); Aristarchus read καιροσέων (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 7.107); only here in Homer
uncontracted gen. pl. (Attic ὀθονῶν); genitive of separation with ἀπολείβεται

'drips off', only here in Homer; Nitzsch, after Plutarch, took it of a weave so close that oil does not soak in; most take the 'oil' as the gloss of the cloth, as Iliad 18.595–596; Merry thinks the strong phrase points to real oil, used in dressing cloth (Merry on 7.107)

108.n: epic ὅσσος = ὅσος; adverbial, answered by ὥς (109) (Merry on 7.109)

110.n: genitive with τεχνῆσσαι, matching νῆα … ἐλαυνέμεν (109) as τεχνῆσσαι matches ἴδριες (108) (Merry on 7.110); La Roche's reading, from two Vienna manuscripts, for the common ἱστόν, which went with the infinitive τεχνῆσαι (Merry's critical note on 7.110)

contracted from τεχνήεσσαι, as τιμῆντα Iliad 18.475: 'skilled'; ἐστί understood; Bekker's reading, for the vulgate infinitive τεχνῆσαι 'to work', though Homer has only the middle τεχνάομαι (Merry on 7.110 and critical note); τεχνήεντες again 8.297
adverbial πέρι (accent thrown back): 'exceedingly, beyond others', as 2.116
giver of skill in women's work, as 2.116–117 and 20.72

111.n: women's work, weaving above all; object of ἐπίστασθαι
'know how to, understand', + acc.; with δῶκεν (110); the line = 2.117 (of Penelope)
φρένας ἐσθλάς 'good sense', object of δῶκεν (110) rather than of ἐπίστασθαι

112.n: 'rows of trees', hence 'orchard', as Iliad 14.123: ὄρχος a single row, ὄρχατος the rows together (Bothe, in Merry on 7.112); ἐστί understood

113.n: 'of four γύαι', measures of plowland, as πεντηκοντόγυος 'of fifty acres' Iliad 9.579; again 18.374
adverbial 'round about'; περὶ δʼ ἕρκος as the fence round the vineyard on the shield, Iliad 18.564
perfect passive (Attic reduplication) of ἐλαύνω: 'is drawn, carried round', as ἕρκος ἔλασσε Iliad 18.564
ἀμφότερος 'both' with the suffix -θεν: 'on both sides', i.e. all round

114.n: the first of three scenes, each opened by ἔνθα δέ: the fruit trees (114–121), the vineyard (122–126), the garden beds (127–128) (Merry on 7.122)

perfect with present sense, with a short α in the ending, in Homer only here and λελόγχασι 11.304 (πεφύασι 128) (Merry on 7.114); Herodian's reading, where the manuscripts have πεφύκει (Merry's critical note on 7.114)

114.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. neut.

115.n: 'pear tree'; in apposition to δένδρεα (114); 115–116 again 11.589–590, the trees over Tantalus
'with splendid fruit' (ἀγλαός + καρπός); two-termination adjective; again only 11.589

116.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. fem.

117.n: epic gen. pl. -άων (= τῶν): the trees named in 115–116
οὔ ποτε 'never'; accented before enclitic ποτε
καρπός 'fruit', a different word from καρπός 'wrist'

118.n: genitive of time: χείματος οὐδὲ θέρευς 'neither in winter nor in summer' (Merry on 7.118); χεῖμα 'winter' is not in the Iliad, which has χειμών
Ionic gen. -ευς (= θέρους); genitive of time
'lasting the year through' (ἐπί + ἔτος), agreeing with καρπός (117) and added in explanation (Merry on 7.118); only here in Homer

119.n: the feminine of an adjective ζεφύριος 'of the west wind', used as a noun ('the west breeze'), as Merry on 7.119 takes it; the Iliad has Ζέφυρος; its short first syllable is scanned long at the head of the line, as ἐπίτονος at 12.423 (Merry on 7.119); only here in Homer

119.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

120.n: = ἐπί: one after another, fruit following fruit
of fruit, 'ripens to the full'; understood again with μῆλον, σταφυλή and σῦκον (120–121)

121.n: 'bunch of grapes' (not σταφύλη 'level', Iliad 2.765); the grapes are unexpected among the orchard trees, as vines belong to the vineyard of 122 (Merry on 7.122)
the fruit of the συκέη (116); only here in Homer

122.n: ἔνθα δέ opens each scene of the ὄρχατος: the fruit trees (114), the vineyard here, the garden beds (127) (Merry on 7.122)

ῥιζόω 'make to take root': 'is planted' (the scholia), or rather 'is firmly fixed', perhaps of the deep foundations of its winepress and of a trench dug round it, cf. ἐρρίζωσεν 13.163, of the ship fixed to the sea floor (Merry on 7.122)

123.n: article used as relative (= ἧς): the vineyard; partitive with ἕτερον

agrees with θειλόπεδον, though set against ἑτέρας (124); ἕτερον … ἑτέρας divide one scene, grapes drying on the vine and grapes being gathered, the treading (125) is a second, the unripe grapes (125–126) a third (Merry on 7.123)

'a sunny place' where grapes are dried (probably εἵλη 'warmth of the sun' + πέδον 'ground'); subject of τέρσεται, where properly the grapes are dried: bunches left on the vine for raisin wine (Merry on 7.123); some read εἱλόπεδον, Bekker μέν θʼ εἱλόπεδον (Merry's critical note on 7.123); only here in Homer

124.n: epic ἠέλιος = ἥλιος; dative of means
epic diectasis (= τρυγῶσι): 'gather the vintage', as Iliad 18.566

125.n: σταφυλάς understood; ἄλλος marks a new scene, where ἕτερος marks the two parts of one (Merry on 7.123)
uncontracted; 'tread (grapes)', cf. ἀτραπός 'path' and English 'tramp': the whole scene of the winepress in two words (Merry on 7.125); only here in Homer
in the foreground: rows of vines whose grapes are still unripe (Merry on 7.125)
'unripe grape'; second accent from enclitic εἰσιν; only here in Homer

126.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. fem.
126.n: 'letting fall': some just rid of their blossom, or they would not yet be grapes, as if ἕτεραι μέν stood before it to answer ἕτεραι δʼ (Merry on 7.125)

'are beginning to color' with the dark hue of ripening grapes (ὑπο- 'slightly' + περκάζω, cf. περκνός 'dusky'); a finite verb where the sentence leads one to expect a participle answering ἀφιεῖσαι (Merry on 7.126); only here in Homer

127.n: the third scene, the garden, bordering on the vineyard (Merry on 7.127)
'well ordered' (κοσμέω 'set in order'); only here in Homer
properly 'leek beds' (πράσον 'leek'): a kitchen garden of herbs, not flowers, whose cultivation Homer never mentions (Merry on 7.127); again 24.247
a row of vines: the beds skirt the outermost row of the vineyard (Merry on 7.127); again 24.341

128.n: intransitive perfect with present sense, 'are grown'; epic -ᾱσι, beside πεφύκᾰσι 114 (Merry on 7.114)

128.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. fem.
128.n: epic diectasis (= γανῶσαι): 'gleaming' with fresh green (Merry on 7.127)

129.n: epic δύω = δύο, with plural κρῆναι
ἡ μέν … ἡ δʼ (130) 'one … the other'
the enclosure of the garden beds of 127 (Merry on 7.129)

130.n: 'is spread about': 'is led in rills' (Merry on 7.130)
ἕτερος with the suffix -θεν; here 'over against it', as Iliad 6.247, facing the first spring, not necessarily far from it (Merry on 7.130)
intransitive, 'sends (its water)', i.e. flows, as 11.239 of a river: led under the threshold of the court, it perhaps rose in a basin in the courtyard (Merry on 7.130)

131.n: from the spring itself, before it passed under the threshold (Merry on 7.130)
middle 'draw water for oneself'; ὅθεν ὑδρεύοντο πολῖται again 17.206
contracted form of πολιήτης, as Iliad 22.429

132.n: = τοῖα, predicate: 'such were …', closing the description of the house and its grounds

133.n: ἔνθα στὰς θηεῖτο as 5.75 (Hermes before Calypso's cave)

133.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

133.n: Ionic θηέομαι = θεάομαι; unaugmented imperfect, contracted (from θηέετο)

135.n: with εἴσω, 'into the house'; or with οὐδόν, 'the threshold of the house'

136.n: Φαιήκων ἡγήτορες ἠδὲ μέδοντες again 186, as the Achaeans' 'leaders and rulers', Iliad 2.79
participle of μέδω 'rule', used as a noun

137.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. pl. masc.

137.n: epic dat. pl. -εσσι(ν); dative of means
Hermes: title traditionally 'slayer of Argus'; sense disputed

138.n: 'to him last' before going to bed: the scholia explain it of Hermes as escort of dreams or giver of sleep, whose wand charms men's eyes (5.47); Nitzsch, of Hermes as guardian of the house for the night (Merry on 7.138)
with the optative of repeated action: 'whenever'
epic 3 pl. -αίατο (= μνήσαιντο); optative of repeated action in past time; + gen.

139.n: Odysseus, named at the end of the line
epic διά + acc. of the space crossed

140.n: = ἠέρα, epic acc. of ἀήρ, feminine in Homer: 'mist'

140.n: 'having (on him)', as one has clothes or armor, εἵματα ἔχειν 17.24, τεύχεα ἔχειν Iliad 10.440 (Merry on 7.140)

141.n: = ἵκετο; + acc. of the persons reached
wife of Alcinous and daughter of his brother Rhexenor (63–66)

142.n: with γούνασι, 'round the knees', or in tmesis with βάλε: the suppliant's clasp, as Nausicaa had bidden (6.310–311)

143.n: epic gen. -οιο; not simply 'from him' but 'from the hero himself', now visible; genitive of separation with πάλιν χύτο, as with πάλιν τράπεθʼ Iliad 18.138 (Merry on 7.143)
athematic aorist middle (ἐχύμην), unaugmented, passive in sense: 'was poured back'
'spoken by a god' (θεός + φημί), hence 'set by a god', 'divine'; two-termination adjective, with ἀήρ

144.n: 'in silence', as ἄνεῳ … ἐγένοντο Iliad 3.84; Aristarchus and his school took the word as an adverb, not as an adjective (Apollonius, in Merry's critical note on 7.144)
after its noun, accent thrown back (anastrophe)

144.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
144.n: aorist: a hush fell the moment they caught sight of him; the present ὁρόωντες (145) of their continued gazing (Merry on 7.144)

145.n: unaugmented (= ἐθαύμαζον): they had not seen him approach (scholia, in Merry on 7.144)

145.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

145.n: Odysseus, named at the end of the line
unaugmented; the reading of Aristarchus, where the vulgate has δʼ ἐλλιτάνευεν (Merry's critical note on 7.145)

146.n: son of Nausithous and brother of Alcinous, killed by Apollo (63–66); the name is the epithet ῥηξήνωρ 'breaker of men', of Achilles at Iliad 7.228

147.n: the line after 5.449, to the river god (σόν τε ῥόον)

present with perfect sense; + acc. of the goal

147.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

148.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); or relative, 'to whom'
used as a noun: 'blessings, prosperity'; ὄλβια δοῖεν stands alone at 8.413 (Merry on 7.148)

149.n: epic inf. -έμεναι (= ζῆν); explanatory, 'prosperity to live in', 'throughout their life', rather than governed by δοῖεν (Merry on 7.148)
emphatic: to their own children, not to strangers (Merry on 7.150)
optative of wish: 'hand over, leave'; the singular, with ἕκαστος, is the reading of Aristarchus' texts, some scholia have ἐπιτρέψειαν (Merry's critical note on 7.149)

150.n: the royal domain granted by the people, the τέμενος (cf. 6.293) (Merry on 7.150)
= τε; τ → θ before rough breathing

150.p: indef. rel. pron. · acc. sg. neut.
150.n: ὅ τι written apart (= ὅτι, neut. of ὅστις): 'whatever'

150.p: indef. rel. pron. · acc. sg. neut.

151.n: 'hasten', addressed to the king and queen and the lords
= πατρίδα; used as a noun: 'native land'; acc. of the goal without a preposition

152.n: comparative (Attic θᾶττον), almost 'the sooner the better'; often with imperatives, here rather with ἱκέσθαι (Merry on 7.152)
with δηθά: 'now for a long time'
accent thrown back (anastrophe): placed after its noun; the half-line as 1.49
present of what has gone on for a long time and still goes on

153.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

153.n: = κατά; in tmesis with ἕζετο (καθέζομαι 'sit down')
Ionic -η (Attic ἐσχάρα); he sits in the posture of a suppliant, though in Homer no sanctity attaches to the hearth (Ameis, in Merry on 7.153)
epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν); 'dust', here the ashes of the hearth

154.n: οἱ δʼ ἄρα πάντες ἀκὴν ἐγένοντο σιωπῇ as Iliad 9.29

155.n: ὀψὲ δὲ δή 'at long last', as Iliad 9.432
used like an adjective with ἥρως
the eldest of the Phaeacians (156); again 11.342; one scholium records the reading Ἁλιθέρσης (Merry's critical note on 7.155)

156.n: partitive with ὅς, not governed by προγενέστερος (Merry on 7.156)
comparative of προγενής 'born before', standing alone, 'elderly', as γεραίτερος 3.362 (Merry on 7.156); Bekker reads προγενέστατος (Merry's critical note on 7.156); the line again 11.343

157.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι; dative of respect
unaugmented pluperfect (= ἐκέκαστο) with imperfect sense: 'excelled', + dat.
substantive: 'things of old'; accent from enclitic τε; παλαιά τε πολλά τε εἰδώς as 2.188

157.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

158.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
158.n: uncontracted (Attic φρονῶν); ἐὺ φρονέων 'with good intent'

159.n: = μήν, emphatic; οὐ μέν is answered by ἀλλʼ ἄγε (162) (Merry on 7.159); a scholium records οὐ μὲν καὶ τό γε (Merry's critical note on 7.159)
explained by the infinitive ἧσθαι (160) (Merry on 7.159)
comparative of καλός, ἐστί understood: no better, 'not more honorable', than the Phaeacians' usual welcome of strangers (Merry on 7.159)

160.n: Ionic ξεῖνος = ξένος; subject of ἧσθαι

161.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
161.n: epic ποτι- = προσ-; root-aorist participle with present sense 'expecting'
epic diectasis (= ἰσχανῶνται); a lengthened form of ἴσχω: 'are putting constraint on themselves' (Merry on 7.161)

163.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

163.n: epic dat. pl. -εσσι; dative with κέλευσον

164.n: 'mix (the wine) with water', as ἀνὰ … κέρασσε 3.390 (Merry on 7.164); aorist from the stem κρη- (cf. ἄκρητος 'unmixed'); only here in Homer

165.n: short-vowel subjunctive (= σπείσωμεν), after ἵνα; 164–165 again 180–181
= τε; τ → θ before rough breathing: of what is always so
epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν); with ἅμʼ … ὀπηδεῖ
= ἅμα; ἅμʼ ὀπηδεῖ 'goes along with, attends'
epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); 'revered', as ἱκέταο … αἰδοίοιο (Iliad 21.75); suppliants are αἰδοῖοι, 'to be respected' (5.447)

166.p: verb · pres. part. act. gen. pl. neut.
166.n: epic ἐών = ὤν; partitive: 'of the things within', as παρεόντων (176)

167.n: ἱερὸν μένος Ἀλκινόοιο, a periphrasis for Alcinous himself, as ἱερὴ ἲς Τηλεμάχοιο 2.409; often in Books 8 and 13

168.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

168.n: 'of intricate cunning' (ποικίλος + μῆτις); δαΐφρονα ποικιλομήτην as Iliad 11.482

169.n: epic -φι(ν), here as genitive with ἀπό; formed as if from the o-declension, as 5.59

170.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
170.n: transitive aorist: he gives the stranger his son's seat
son of Alcinous; not the Trojan son of Antenor, Iliad 15.516

171.n: accent from enclitic μιν; δέ … μιν in place of a second relative, as μάλιστα δέ μιν φιλέεσκε Iliad 3.388 (Merry on 7.171)
iter. (-σκ-), uncontracted -εε-; the subject is his father, Alcinous (Merry on 7.171)

172.n: epic aorist ἔχευα (Attic ἐπέχεε): poured the water over the hands

172.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

173.n: held under the hands to catch the water

174.n: epic -σσ-; 'stretched out', i.e. set (the table) in place; on the scholium that rejects this line see 232

175.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. fem.
verb · pres. part. act. gen. pl. neut.

177.n: the line after 6.249 (and 5.94, of Hermes); after it one manuscript adds αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ δείπνησε καὶ ἤραρε θυμὸν ἐδωδῇ (Merry's critical note on 7.177)
Odysseus, named at the end of the line
imperfect of ἔσθω, by-form of ἐσθίω; in Homer only in this formula (5.94, 6.249, here)

178.n: μένος Ἀλκινόοιο, periphrasis for Alcinous, as 167; the line again 13.49

179.n: the herald of Alcinous, again 182, 8.65, 13.50, 13.53; a speaking name (πόντος 'sea' + νόος 'mind'), like many Phaeacian names
Ionic κρητήρ = κρατήρ, the mixing bowl

179.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
179.n: epic -σσ-; 'having mixed (the wine in) the bowl', the participle sharing the command: 'mix and serve'

181.n: = τε; τ → θ before rough breathing: of what is always so
epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν); with ἅμʼ … ὀπηδεῖ
= ἅμα; ἅμʼ ὀπηδεῖ 'goes along with, attends'

182.n: 'honey-hearted', Tennyson's rendering, which gives the wine a kind of personality (Merry on 7.182); lit. 'sweet to the mind', as Iliad 6.264
from κιρνάω (κίρνημι), an epic present of κεράννυμι 'mix'; μελίφρονα οἶνον ἐκίρνα again 10.356, 13.53

183.n: unaugmented (= ἐνώμησεν); the line after Iliad 1.471 (plural)
a scholium marks a short pause after it (Merry's critical note on 7.183)

183.g: first pouring drops for the libation
183.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

184.n: unaugmented (= ἔσπεισαν); second accent from enclitic τʼ
2nd aorist ἔπιον; second accent from enclitic θʼ
= τε; τ → θ before rough breathing
singular for the hearts of all

185.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); dative with μετέειπε; the line again 8.25
= δέ, opening the main clause after ἐπεί (184)

186.n: reduplicated aorist imperative; the line again 8.26, 8.97, 8.387, 8.536
participle of μέδω 'rule', used as a noun

187.n: article used as relative: 'the things which'

188.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.

188.n: 'go to rest'; taken by some as an aorist imperative, by others as a desiderative (Merry on 7.188); cf. κακκείοντες 229

188.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

189.n: ἠώς with the suffix -θεν: 'from dawn on', i.e. at daybreak

293.n: with the optative: potential; scanned long, since ἔλποιο had the digamma (Merry on 7.293)
potential optative with ἄν; + acc. and inf. ἐρξέμεν (294)

293.p: verb · aor. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

294.n: epic infinitive -έμεν, probably aorist (as ἀξέμεν), which the scholia render πρᾶξαι, though Eustathius' ἔρξειν takes it as future (Merry on 7.294); Merry thinks the line awkward: ἀντιάσαντα ends line and sense at 6.193, 14.511, Iliad 10.551, so that ἐρξέμεν may have been added, with a commonplace to fill the verse (Merry's critical note on 7.294)
uncontracted (Attic ἀφραδοῦσι): 'act without thought' (ἀ- + φράζομαι); in Homer only here and Iliad 9.32

295.n: the relative opening a new sentence: 'and she'
'fiery-looking', used of the gleam of wine, bronze and smoke (Merry on 7.295)

296.n: = λοῦσε, unaugmented (= ἔλουσε): she had him bathed (6.210), though he washed himself (6.218–224)
= εἵματα; the answer to Arete's question (238)

297.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
297.n: second accent from enclitic περ; concessive with περ
Ionic ἀληθείη = ἀλήθεια; predicative to ταῦτα: 'as the truth' (Merry on 7.297)

298.n: Odysseus; the line again 308, 11.347, 13.3, as Iliad 20.199 (Aeneas)
unaugmented (= ἐφώνησε); second accent from enclitic τε

299.n: ἦ τοι (= ἤτοι) with μέν, answered by σὺ δʼ (301)
second accent from enclitic γʼ; explained by οὕνεκα … (300–301); τοῦτό γʼ ἐναίσιμον οὐκ ἐνόησε as 2.122

300.n: παῖς of a daughter, feminine with ἐμή
= οὗ ἕνεκα 'in that'; second accent from enclitic σʼ

301.n: ἐς ἡμέτερον, sc. δῶμα, as εἰς ἡμέτερον 2.55; the scholia read ἡμετέρου, an Attic turn like ἐς διδασκάλου (Merry's critical note on 7.301)
= δέ, answering μέν (299): this gives the reason she was wrong not to bring him (Merry on 7.301)
'came as a suppliant to', + acc.; as 292

302.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

303.n: vocative, same form as the nominative; to the king
the particle, or σοι; Merry prints μή μοι
= τοὔνεκα; crasis of τοῦ ἕνεκα 'on that account'

304.n: she had bidden him follow with the handmaids through the fields (6.259–261), then wait in Athena's grove (6.291–299)

305.n: unaugmented (= ἤθελον): 'I was not willing'; Eustathius remarks that Odysseus is plainly lying here, as a wise man will when the moment calls for it (Merry on 7.305): it was Nausicaa who had him wait apart (6.262–299)

305.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
305.n: aorist: the sudden fear, beside the present αἰσχυνόμενος, the lasting modesty (Merry on 7.305)

305.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
305.n: middle 'feeling shame'; second accent from enclitic τε

306.n: dative of the person: 'your heart'; with ἰδόντι
epic -σσ- aorist: 'be indignant'; Düntzer takes it of the knitted brow (ἐπισκύνιον) (Merry on 7.305)

306.p: verb · aor. part. act. dat. sg. masc.
306.n: agrees with σοί: 'should you see me following her', taking up ἕπεσθαι (Merry on 7.306)

307.n: 'quick to anger, touchy' (δυσ- + ζηλ-, cf. ζέω 'boil') (Merry on 7.307); masculine by sense with φῦλα; only here in Homer
= φῦλα; with the masculine δύσζηλοι, agreement by sense, for which Nitzsch compares φῦλα γυναικῶν … σύμφοροι, Hesiod, Theogony 593 (Merry on 7.307)

308.n: unaugmented (= ἐφώνησε); second accent from enclitic τε

309.n: accent from enclitic μοι; sc. ἐστί
predicate, explained by the infinitive κεχολῶσθαι (310), as τοῖοι ἀμυνέμεν 2.60 (Merry on 7.309)

310.n: contracted (= ἀμείνονα); predicate: 'fair measure in all things is best' (Merry on 7.310)
used as a noun: 'what is due, right' (αἶσα 'portion')

311.n: αἲ γάρ, here with the infinitive ἐχέμεν (313), not the optative: the wish passes into a prayer (Merry on 7.311); epic αἰ = εἰ; the line = 4.341, Iliad 2.371; Aristarchus doubted that 311–316 are Homer's: how could Alcinous offer his daughter to a man he does not know? (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 7.311–316)

312.n: nominative, as if a finite verb followed

312.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

312.n: antecedent of ἅ: τά τε φρονέων 'feeling as I feel', that is, agreeing to stay (Merry on 7.312)

312.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

313.n: epic inf. -έμεν (= ἔχειν): 'have (as wife)'; infinitive after αἲ γάρ, as 24.376; the infinitive of a prayer, as Iliad 7.179 (Merry on 7.311)

314.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

314.n: = κε; with the optative δοίην: potential; Hermann's correction for the manuscripts' δέ τʼ, adopted by Bekker, La Roche and Nauck, and supported by a reading κἀγώ (Merry's critical note on 7.314)

315.n: accent from enclitic κʼ; εἰ κε + optative

315.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

316.n: μή with the optative of wish: 'may it not'; that is, that any Phaeacian should detain you (Merry on 7.316)

317.n: ἐς τόδʼ … αὔριον ἐς: 'for a certain day, and that tomorrow' (Merry on 7.317)
subjunctive of οἶδα, with present sense

318.n: properly the neuter of an adjective, here governed by ἐς (Merry on 7.317)
placed after its word; modern editors since Nitzsch divide here, but most manuscripts and Eustathius after αὔριον, reading ἐς τῆμος δέ 'until then' (Merry's critical note on 7.318)
'at that time': all the while, during the voyage, or simply 'when tomorrow comes' (Merry on 7.318)

318.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.
318.n: perfect stem δεδμη- (cf. δάμνημι) 'tame, overpower'; so he sleeps on the voyage, 13.79–80

319.n: middle of λέγω 'lay': 'lie down' (cf. λέχος 'bed'); uncontracted 2 sg. -εαι (= λέξῃ)
epic future ἐλόω with diectasis (= ἐλῶσι): 'will row (you) over the calm', as πόντον ἐλαύνοντες Iliad 7.6 (Merry on 7.319); the scholia give both ἐλάσουσι and ἐλάωσι (Merry's critical note on 7.319)
the calm sea, accusative of the way traveled

320.n: accent from enclitic πού; εἴ που 'if anywhere': wherever else he wishes to go

321.n: accent from enclitic περ; εἴ περ καί 'even if'
epic πολλόν = πολύ, adverbial with the comparative: 'by far'
comparative of ἑκάς 'far', + gen. of comparison Εὐβοίης; only here in Homer (superlative ἑκαστάτω Iliad 10.113)
Ionic gen. -ης; genitive of comparison; the great island along the coast of Boeotia and Attica (Iliad 2.535)

322.n: article used as relative; accented before enclitic περ
superlative of τῆλε 'far', as ἑκαστάτω of ἑκάς; only here in Homer
accented before enclitic μιν; those of our people (323) who
unaugmented middle aorist (= εἴδοντο), same sense as active

323.n: brother of Minos (Iliad 14.322); in the Odyssey he dwells in the Elysian plain (4.564); the legend of this voyage is otherwise unknown, and Merry wonders whether Scheria was thought to lie near Elysium (Merry on 7.323)

324.p: verb · fut. part. mid. acc. sg. masc.
324.n: future participle of purpose (ἐπόψομαι, from ἐφοράω): 'to see, visit'
the giant punished in Hades for assaulting Leto (11.576–581); Eustathius guesses that Rhadamanthus went to see his size, or, being just, to chasten him (Merry on 7.323)
patronymic adjective of Γαῖα 'Earth', with υἱόν, as Ποιάντιον υἱόν 3.190 (Merry on 7.324); Tityus is Γαίης … υἱός at 11.576; only here in Homer

325.n: unaugmented, epic -σσ- (= ἐτέλεσαν): 'finished (the voyage)'; τελέω of the journey accomplished, ἀπανύω (326) of arrival at the goal (Merry on 7.325)

326.n: with αὐτῷ: 'on that very day', nearly the Attic ὁ αὐτός (Merry on 7.326)
'accomplished (the way) back', with οἴκαδε (Merry on 7.325); a gloss in one manuscript and the lemma of a scholion have ἀπήγαγον (Merry's critical note on 7.326); only here in Homer

327.n: epic ὅσσος (double σ); adverbial neuter, as ὄφρʼ ἐῢ εἰδῇς ὅσσον φέρτερός εἰμι, Iliad 1.185–186
feminine, agreeing with the nearer subject νῆες (328), though it covers κοῦροι too

328.n: infinitive of respect with ἄρισται: 'best at tossing up' (ἀνά + ῥίπτω); ἀνερρίπτουν ἅλα πηδῷ 13.78, of the same crew
'oar-blade' (cf. πηδάλιον 'steering oar'), perhaps from πηδάω 'leap', the blade springing from the water at the end of the stroke (Merry on 7.328); in Homer only here and 13.78

330.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

330.n: ἔπος τʼ ἔφατʼ 'spoke a word'; the half-line as 4.610, 5.181; for it the scholia preserve εἶπε πρὸς ὃν μεγαλήτορα θυμόν and ἰδὼν εἰς οὐρανὸν εὐρύν (Merry's critical note on 7.330)

331.n: optative of wish with αἴθε; epic -ειε(ν); its subject Ἀλκίνοος (332)

332.n: subject of τελευτήσειεν (331), held back to the next line
accent from enclitic κεν; answered by ἐγὼ δέ (333)
epic κεν = ἄν; with the optative εἴη (333): 'then … would be'
'over' the earth: his fame 'would be spread throughout the world' (Merry on 7.332)

333.n: predicate; 'inextinguishable', a word used of fire; two-termination adjective
2nd aorist ἱκόμην; + acc. of the place reached

335.n: reduplicated aorist of κέλομαι; + dat. and inf. θέμεναι (336)
epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); dative with κέκλετο

336.n: = δέμνια 'bedsteads, beds', always plural; 336–339 = 4.297–300 (Helen's orders), Iliad 24.644–647 (Achilles')
the open portico along the court, the sleeping place of guests

337.n: uncontracted 2nd aorist infinitive (= ἐμβαλεῖν): 'put on' the beds

338.n: the thick woolen cloak, here for covering
epic infinitive -μεναι (= ἐνθεῖναι): 'put on' the beds
'woolly, thick'; a different word from οὖλος 'baneful'
aorist middle of ἕννυμι 'clothe': 'to wrap themselves in'; infinitive of purpose

339.n: 'torch', a by-form of δαΐς, used collectively; in Homer only in this line and its repetitions (Iliad 24.647; Odyssey 4.300, 22.497, and 23.294)

339.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. fem.

340.n: unaugmented (= ἐστόρεσαν); it takes up the work of 336–338 (Merry on 7.340); the line again 23.291
epic πυκινός = πυκνός: 'firmly framed', of the bedstead (Merry on 7.340)

340.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. fem.
340.n: 'busily, in haste'; in Homer only in the feminine participle, here, 23.291 and Iliad 24.648 (Merry on 7.340)

341.n: = δέ, in the main clause after ἐπεί (340)

341.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. fem.

342.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
342.n: 'going to lie down' (cf. κεῖμαι), with future sense; the shorter form of κείων, only here (Merry on 7.342)
epic τοι = σοι; dative of advantage: 'for you'

343.n: 'welcome' (ἀσπάζομαι); predicate, with κοιμηθῆναι as subject; in Homer only in the Odyssey
epic aorist ἐεισάμην of εἴδομαι 'seem' (not εἶμι 'go')
passive in middle sense: 'to lie down to sleep'

344.n: Odysseus, named at the end of the line

345.n: 'bored with holes' for the bed-cords; the line = 3.399, of Telemachus at Pylos
epic dat. pl. -εσσι(ν); plural for one bed
the open portico along the court, the sleeping place of guests

346.n: root aorist middle of λέγω 'lay': 'lay down' (cf. λέχος 'bed'); μυχῷ δόμου ὑψηλοῖο as 3.402, 4.304
dative of place: 'in the inmost part'

347.n: 'mistress (of the house)', in apposition to γυνή, as 53; the line nearly 3.403; in Homer only in the Odyssey
unaugmented (= ἐπόρσυνε): 'made ready', i.e. shared, as 3.403; Aristarchus' copies read πόρσαινε (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 7.347)
